core.fantasy: You are the governor of a Roman-era province who turns empty islands into prosperous, interlocking cities, and chooses how far the local culture becomes Roman.
pillars: Population tiers whose needs keep growing
Beautiful, dense cities you can zoom into street by street
core.signature_moment: Zooming from the whole province, ships and chains humming, down into a single street where the residents you just satisfied are walking, trading and celebrating.
anti_goals: no direct control of individual citizens

signatures.description: Residences belong to tiers; each tier needs more goods and services, and a house that has what the next tier needs can be upgraded.
Each tier supplies its own workforce, and production buildings need a particular tier's workers, so a city that upgrades everyone starves its lower chains.
Raw goods grow on fertile land of a particular island; processing buildings turn them into goods; ships carry them along trade routes to where they are needed.
Public buildings (market, baths, temples) serve houses within a reach measured along roads.
A second province with a local culture where the player decides how far to Romanise or keep local ways, changing goods and needs.
Its specific provinces, tier names, characters, story, music, art and UI.

take.setting: Four kinds of household (settlers, townsfolk, artisans, patrons) with cumulative needs; a block grows into the next kind when it has everything that kind needs.
Each kind does its own work; the council holds some blocks back when their work would go undone.
Chains run across the countryside around the town tile, on the real soil (alluvium, terra rossa, clay, pasture, woods), worked by people who walk out.
Service reach is walking time over the real streets and slopes.
